Y Message from the Board of Directors 


1984 will be remembered as a year of vision 
and direction-setting in our YMCA. Thanks to 
the countless hours of dedicated work of our 
volunteers and staff, we were able to 
establish a Strategic Plan of development for 
the Montreal YMCA. Our updated Mission 
Statement which guides principles, goals and 
key thrusts in programs, human resources, 
finance, facilities, and our public image will 
foster a strong common vision and sense of 
direction for the next three years. 

As we review the year, we are particularly 

proud that: 

e Our YMCA enjoyed an operating surplus of 
$114,000, despite a troubled economy; 

¢ Kamp Kanawana celebrated its 75th year 
of service. More than 34,000 people have 
benefited over the years from their involve- 
ment at Kanawana; 

e Our Foundation, under the Chairmanship 
of Jack H. Warren, has worked hard to lay 
the groundwork for a much needed major 
Capital Development Program to com- 
mence in 1985; 


Victor M. Drury 


e We renewed our agreement with Centraide 
for another three years; 
e Participation in all our programs continued 
to increase; 
e We received a mandate from the National 
Council of YMCAs of Canada (who signed 
a contract with the Federal Government) to 
develop and oversee a major program for 
unemployed youth in ten YMCAs across 
the country. 
We actively participated in Voyage 84, the 
National Conference of YMCAs of Canada 
held in Halifax. This was the first national 
gathering since 1976, and over five hun- 
dred representatives from some seventy 
Associations along with many of our Inter- 
national colleagues attended. We will con- 
tinue to support and strengthen our na- 
tional ties. This will in turn benefit our 
Association. 
This has been a year of tremendous con- 
solidation for us and the beginning of a new 
thrust to translate the Y’s philosophy and 
plans into action. 
We are an organization of people committed 
to the betterment of our community, and 
count on our members, volunteers and 
friends to achieve our mission. 


hu 


Victor M. Drury 


President 


0, one 


Sol Kasimer 


Director general 


Y Our Mission 


“The Montreal YMCA is a partnership of 
volunteers and staff committed to the fulfil- 
ment of people in spirit, mind and body, and 
to the development of self-reliance in the in- 
dividual and the community. 
Through its actions, programs and services, 
the Montreal YMCA will reflect the needs and 
aspirations of the community and will work 
with individuals, local communities and com- 
munities in developing countries in achieving 
social justice and control of their 
environments’’. 

Concordia, 1984

7 Involvement in the Community 


“Man is not a body nor a mind nor a spirit 
but is a wonderful combination of these 
elements of personality’. 


Harold C. Cross 


Highlights 


Operating budget of $11,518,000 

1,000 employees (750 part-time) 

Over 2,150 volunteers 

Assets of $16,858,000 

78,275 registered program participants and 
over 40,000 non-registered participants. 


Young and old, men and women, children 
and teens all share their experiences and 
ideals without distinction of language, race 
or creed. 


The YMCA is in the community. 


What is the YMCA? 


The Montreal YMCA is one of the largest non-profit organizations based on the efforts of 
volunteers. Dedicated to the betterment of the person and the community, the Montreal YMCA 
is an integral part of the daily lives of more than 100,000 Montrealers who participate in a wide 
range of quality programs at our nine branches and summer camp.
